name: Starship Travel Events Table
notes: Roll D100 if you opt to travel with your own ship (not when traveling commercially). If an event does not line up well with the story, you can change the narration while retaining the mechanical effects. Several events cause the loss of ship Hull Points, which affects your ability to take off from planets (p.59).

rows.detail: Rocky debris everywhere. If you wish to avoid it, roll 1D6, requiring a 5+ to chart a safe path; if successful, roll again on this table. To go through the field, select a crew member and roll 1D6+Savvy three times, requiring a 4+ to succeed each time. Each failed roll inflicts 1D6 Hull Point damage to the ship.

Lose 1 story point as you drift through empty space, then roll again on this table. If your ship is currently suffering from Hull Point damage, a random crew member must roll on the Injury Table, as system failures cause life support malfunctions across the vessel.

Pirates. Intimidation might work: select a crew member and roll 1D6+Savvy; a 6+ is required to avoid conflict. Otherwise, set up a battle in cramped territory using the Criminal Elements Encounter Table (p.94). Enemy numbers: roll 3D6 and pick the highest die (crew size 5: 2D6 pick highest; crew size 4: 1D6), add the numbers indicated in the enemy table, +1 extra figure. There is no objective. If you lose, you lose all credits and everything in your Stash, though you can keep the ship. If you win, you get the normal rewards for winning an Opportunity mission (p.120), plus a bonus roll on the Loot Table. This battle is an out-of-sequence encounter and does not count as the main Battle stage.
You find an old wreck drifting through empty space. Scanning it, you get 2 rolls on the Gear Subtable (p.132). Both items are damaged and need to be Repaired.

Select 3 crew members and have each roll 1D6+Savvy. A 6+ is required for success. For each failure, you are grounded on the next world for one campaign turn while the drive is reset. Taking off before the drive is reset inflicts 2D6 Hull Point damage to the ship.
Select a crew member of choice and add +1 XP. The crew can Repair 1 damaged item with no roll required.

If you come to their aid, roll 1D6. 1: The ship's drive detonates; your ship suffers 1D6+1 Hull Point damage. 2: You only find drifting wreckage. 3-4: You can rescue a crew member; treat this as the Escape Pod event. 5-6: Help save the ship from a drive malfunction: select a crew member and roll 1D6+Savvy, 7+ required, three attempts allowed. If you succeed, roll three times on the gear loot table. If you fail, the drive detonates and your ship is damaged as if you had rolled a 1.

A Unity patrol vessel hails you. Roll 1D6-3 twice. Each die that scores above a 0 results in that number of items being confiscated as contraband (any items carried or in your Stash). Due to the military presence, the next world you visit cannot be Invaded.

A crew member sees a strange manifestation in space and adds +1 Luck (if they are able). This event can only happen once in a campaign; treat as nothing happening if it happens again. If you have a Precursor in the crew, add +1 story point as well.

If you opt to rescue them, roll 1D6. 1: A wanted criminal. If you let them go on the next world, the next time you make a new Rival, roll 4+ on 1D6 to immediately remove it. If you turn them in, claim 1D6 credits but get a Rival from their old gang. 2-3: They reward you with 1D3 credits and a roll on the Loot Table when you arrive on the nearest world. 4: Add 1 Quest Rumor and 1 story point. 5: They are willing to join your crew; roll up a new character with no equipment. 6: As 5, but the character begins play with 10 XP as yet unspent.
A crew member gets Injured while doing a routine maintenance task. They must rest up for one campaign turn to recover from the Injury, and one item they carry is damaged.
Local conditions force you to jump to the very edge of the system and approach under standard drives. Any Injured crew may rest for one campaign turn.
You can Repair one damaged item.
Roll 1D6. On a 1-2, a random crew member earns +3 XP. On a 3-4, a random crew member earns +2 XP and a second random crew member earns +1 XP. On a 5-6, three random crew each earn +1 XP.

rows.result: Locked in the library data by night
rows.detail: You can roll up the planetary info (problems, conveniences, licensing requirements) for three worlds and select which you wish to visit, but you must visit one of the three generated. All three generated worlds remain in the campaign, and can be visited later.
